In 1873 the French writer Jules Verne wrote a famous novel,
Around the World in Eighty Days
Its hero, an English gentleman called Phileas Fogg, makes a bet with his friends.
He says he can travel around the whole world in just eighty days.
Fogg leaves London with his servant, Passepartout.
They travel by train and ship across Europe to Egypt, and then to India.
In India there is no railway in one part, so they ride an elephant through the jungle!
They continue to Hong Kong, Japan and across the Pacific Ocean to San Francisco.
Then they cross America by train.
On the way the train is attacked, and Passepartout bravely saves the passengers.
At last they sail across the Atlantic to Britain.
When Fogg arrives in London, he thinks he is one day late and has lost the bet.
But then he realises that, because he travelled east, he has gained a day.
He runs to his club just in time and wins!
Today you can fly around the world in less than two days.
But Fogg's journey shows that travel is about adventures and the people you meet, not only about speed.
